Equivalently, $(\phi,\psi)$ is the block decomposition of the reduced gradient:

$$ \nabla f(\theta,\omega)=\begin{bmatrix}\phi\\
\psi\end{bmatrix}. $$

Since $\hat{D}\succ 0$ , the hill variable can be expressed in terms of the hill force as

$$ \omega=-\theta\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+\hat{D}^{-1}\psi. $$

#### Definition A.10 (River and hill energies).

The reduced loss can be written as

$$ f(\theta,\omega)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\hat{a}\theta^{2}+2\theta\hat{c}^{\top}\omega+\omega^{\top}\hat{D}\omega\right). $$

Using the hill force $\psi=\hat{c}\theta+\hat{D}\omega$ , we have

$$ \psi^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi=\theta^{2}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+2\theta\hat{c}^{\top}\omega+\omega^{\top}\hat{D}\omega. $$

Therefore,

$$ f(\theta,\omega)=\frac{1}{2}\left[\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta^{2}+\psi^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi\right], $$

where the effective river curvature is defined by

$$ \hat{a}_{\rm eff}:=\hat{a}-\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}. $$

We assume throughout that

$$ \hat{a}_{\rm eff}>0. $$

This exact decomposition motivates the river and hill energies

$$ E_{k}:=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}^{2},\qquad H_{k}:=\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}. $$

#### Definition A.11 (Reduced river).

The reduced river is the zero-hill-energy (zero-hill-force) manifold

$$ \mathcal{R}:=\{(\theta,\omega):H=0\}=\{(\theta,\omega):\psi=0\}=\{(\theta,\omega):\omega=-\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\,\theta\}. $$

Furthermore, since $\hat{b}=\hat{c}$ , the river force satisfies

$$ \phi=\hat{a}\theta+\hat{c}^{\top}\omega=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta+\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi. $$

Consequently, along the river manifold $\mathcal{R}$ , where $\psi=0$ , we have $\phi=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta$ . Thus, once the hill force has vanished, the reduced dynamics are governed solely by the effective river curvature $\hat{a}_{\rm eff}$ .

#### Remark A.12 (A brief notation summary).

We summarize the notation used in this section and their relationships in Table 2. We measure river progress by the coordinate $\theta$ , because after eliminating the transverse variables, $\theta$ parametrizes the zero-hill-force valley floor and the remaining loss is $\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta^{2}$ (see (27)). In contrast, the raw hill variable $\omega$ is not a genuine transverse error when $\hat{c}\neq 0$ , since the coupled river itself has $\omega=-\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\theta$ ; hence the intrinsic hill energy must be measured by the hill force $\psi=\hat{c}\theta+\hat{D}\omega$ , or equivalently by the squared $\hat{D}$ -metric distance to the zero-hill-force manifold.

*Table 2: Variables, forces, energies, and reduced discrete iterations in the general PSD case.*

| River Item | River Notation | Hill Item | Hill Notation |
|---|---|---|---|
| River variable | $\theta_{k}=\alpha_{k}-1$ | Hill variable | $\omega_{k}=[\beta_{k},\gamma_{k}]^{\top}$ |
| River force | $\phi_{k}=\hat{a}\theta_{k}+\hat{b}^{\top}\omega_{k}$ | Hill force | $\psi_{k}=\hat{c}\theta_{k}+\hat{D}\omega_{k}$ |
| River energy | $E_{k}=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}^{2}$ | Hill energy | $H_{k}=\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}$ |

For the subsequent local estimates, we restrict the dynamics to the compact box

$$ K_{\underline{\alpha},\overline{\alpha},\underline{\omega},\overline{\omega}}:=\left\{(\theta,\omega)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{2}:\underline{\alpha}\leq 1+\theta\leq\overline{\alpha},\;\underline{\omega}\mathbf{1}_{2}\preceq\omega\preceq\overline{\omega}\mathbf{1}_{2}\right\}, $$

where $\mathbf{1}_{2}=(1,1)^{\top}$ , and $\preceq$ denotes componentwise comparison.

#### A.3.2 Gradient Descent Reduced Dynamics

The reduced GD iteration follows readily from applying an Euler discretization to Lemma A.3:

$$ \begin{cases}\theta_{k+1}=\theta_{k}-4\eta(1+\theta_{k})\phi_{k},\\
\omega_{k+1}=\omega_{k}-4\eta\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}.\end{cases} $$

#### Proposition A.13 (Positivity preservation for reduced GD).

Suppose that at iteration $k$ we have $1+\theta_{k}>0$ and $\omega_{k}\succ 0$ . Assume further that the step size $\eta>0$ is chosen sufficiently small so that, for all $k$ ,

$$ 4\eta|\phi_{k}|<1,\qquad 4\eta\psi_{k}\prec\begin{bmatrix}1\\
1\end{bmatrix}. $$

Then, at iteration $k+1$ , it holds that $1+\theta_{k+1}>0$ and $\omega_{k+1}\succ 0$ .

#### Proof.

From 31, the river-coordinate update can be written as

$$ 1+\theta_{k+1}=(1+\theta_{k})(1-4\eta\phi_{k}). $$

Since $1+\theta_{k}>0$ and $4\eta|\phi_{k}|<1$ , we have $1-4\eta\phi_{k}>0$ , and hence the right-hand side is positive. For each hill coordinate $i\in\{1,2\}$ ,

$$ (\omega_{k+1})_{i}=(\omega_{k})_{i}\bigl(1-4\eta(\psi_{k})_{i}\bigr),\qquad i=1,2. $$

Because $(\omega_{k})_{i}>0$ and $4\eta(\psi_{k})_{i}<1$ , it follows that $1-4\eta(\psi_{k})_{i}>0$ , and therefore $(\omega_{k+1})_{i}>0$ for $i=1,2$ . ∎

#### Proposition A.14 (Hill-energy estimate for reduced GD).

Assume that the GD trajectory remains in the compact box $K_{\underline{\alpha},\overline{\alpha},\underline{\omega},\overline{\omega}}$ . If $0<\eta\leq\frac{\underline{\omega}}{8\nu\overline{\omega}^{2}}$ , then there exists a constant $C_{\rm GD}>0$ , depending only on $\underline{\alpha},\overline{\alpha},\underline{\omega},\overline{\omega},\hat{D},\hat{c}$ and $\eta$ , such that

$$ H_{k+1}\leq(1-2\underline{\omega}\mu\eta)H_{k}+C_{\rm GD}\eta\,\phi_{k}^{2}. $$

Moreover, one admissible choice is

$$ C_{\rm GD}=\frac{8\overline{\alpha}^{2}\|\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\|_{2}^{2}}{\underline{\omega}}+32\overline{\alpha}^{2}\eta\,\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}. $$

#### Proof.

By definition, $\psi_{k+1}=\hat{c}\theta_{k+1}+\hat{D}\omega_{k+1}$ . Using 31, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\psi_{k+1} \displaystyle=\hat{c}\bigl[\theta_{k}-4\eta(1+\theta_{k})\phi_{k}\bigr]+\hat{D}\bigl[\omega_{k}-4\eta\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}\bigr] \displaystyle=\psi_{k}-4\eta\left[\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}+(1+\theta_{k})\hat{c}\,\phi_{k}\right]. $$

Define $r_{k}:=\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}+(1+\theta_{k})\phi_{k}\hat{c}$ . Then $\psi_{k+1}=\psi_{k}-4\eta r_{k}$ , and therefore

$$ \displaystyle H_{k+1}-H_{k} \displaystyle=-8\eta\,\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}+16\eta^{2}r_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}. $$

For the linear term, we have

$$ \displaystyle\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}=\psi_{k}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}+(1+\theta_{k})\phi_{k}\,\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\geq\underline{\omega}\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}-|1+\theta_{k}|\,|\phi_{k}|\,|\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}|, $$

and hence

$$ \displaystyle-8\eta\,\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}\leq-8\underline{\omega}\eta\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}+8\eta|1+\theta_{k}|\,|\phi_{k}|\,|\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}|. $$

For the quadratic term, note that

$$ \displaystyle r_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}=\Bigl[\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}+(1+\theta_{k})\hat{c}\,\phi_{k}\Bigr]^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\Bigl[\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}+(1+\theta_{k})\hat{c}\,\phi_{k}\Bigr] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\bigl\|\hat{D}^{1/2}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}+(1+\theta_{k})\phi_{k}\,\hat{D}^{-1/2}\hat{c}\bigr\|_{2}^{2}\leq 2\|\hat{D}^{1/2}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}+2(1+\theta_{k})^{2}\phi_{k}^{2}\|\hat{D}^{-1/2}\hat{c}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\psi_{k}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})\psi_{k}+2(1+\theta_{k})^{2}\phi_{k}^{2}\,\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\leq 2\nu\overline{\omega}^{2}\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}+2\overline{\alpha}^{2}\phi_{k}^{2}\,\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}. $$

Consequently,

$$ \displaystyle 16\eta^{2}r_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}\leq 32\nu\overline{\omega}^{2}\eta^{2}\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}+32\overline{\alpha}^{2}\eta^{2}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\,\phi_{k}^{2}. $$

Applying Young’s inequality to the mixed term yields

$$ \displaystyle 8\eta|1+\theta_{k}|\,|\phi_{k}|\,|\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}| \displaystyle\leq 2\underline{\omega}\eta\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}+\frac{8\overline{\alpha}^{2}\|\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\|_{2}^{2}}{\underline{\omega}}\eta\phi_{k}^{2}. $$

Combining these estimates we get

$$ \displaystyle H_{k+1}-H_{k}\leq\Bigl(-8\underline{\omega}\eta+2\underline{\omega}\eta+32\nu\overline{\omega}^{2}\eta^{2}\Bigr)\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}+\Biggl(\frac{8\overline{\alpha}^{2}\|\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\|_{2}^{2}}{\underline{\omega}}\eta+32\overline{\alpha}^{2}\eta^{2}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\Biggr)\phi_{k}^{2}. $$

Since $0<\eta\leq\underline{\omega}/(8\nu\overline{\omega}^{2})$ , we have $32\nu\overline{\omega}^{2}\eta^{2}\leq 4\underline{\omega}\eta$ , and thus

$$ H_{k+1}-H_{k}\leq-2\underline{\omega}\eta\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}+C_{\rm GD}\eta\,\phi_{k}^{2}, $$

where one may take

$$ C_{\rm GD}=\frac{8\overline{\alpha}^{2}\|\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\|_{2}^{2}}{\underline{\omega}}+32\overline{\alpha}^{2}\eta\,\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}. $$

Finally, using $\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}\geq\mu H_{k}$ , we conclude that

$$ H_{k+1}\leq(1-2\underline{\omega}\mu\eta)H_{k}+C_{\rm GD}\eta\,\phi_{k}^{2}. $$

The proof is complete. ∎

#### Corollary A.15 (Tail bound for the GD hill energy).

Under the assumptions of the preceding proposition, define $\rho_{\rm GD}:=1-2\underline{\omega}\mu\eta\in(0,1)$ . For any $N\geq 0$ , let $\Phi_{N}:=\sup_{j\geq N}|\phi_{j}|$ . Then, for every $k\geq N$ ,

$$ H_{k}\leq\rho_{\rm GD}^{k-N}H_{N}+\frac{C_{\rm GD}}{2\underline{\omega}\mu}\Phi_{N}^{2}. $$

In particular, if $\phi_{k}\to 0$ , then $H_{k}\to 0$ and hence $\psi_{k}\to 0$ .

#### Proof.

Iterating (32) from $N$ to $k-1$ yields

$$ \displaystyle H_{k}\leq\rho_{\rm GD}^{k-N}H_{N}+C_{\rm GD}\eta\sum_{j=N}^{k-1}\rho_{\rm GD}^{k-1-j}\phi_{j}^{2}\leq\rho_{\rm GD}^{k-N}H_{N}+C_{\rm GD}\eta\Phi_{N}^{2}\sum_{\iota=0}^{k-1-N}\rho_{\rm GD}^{\iota}\leq\rho_{\rm GD}^{k-{N}}H_{N}+\frac{C_{\rm GD}\eta}{1-\rho_{\rm GD}}\Phi_{N}^{2}. $$

Since $1-\rho_{\rm GD}=2\underline{\omega}\mu\eta$ , this implies (33). Finally, if $\phi_{k}\to 0$ , then $\Phi_{N}\to 0$ as $N\to\infty$ , and therefore $H_{k}\to 0$ . ∎

#### Remark A.16 (A Lyapunov perspective on GD).

The GD dynamics admit a natural interpretation from the viewpoint of Lyapunov dissipation. In the region $\alpha>0$ , $\beta\geq 0$ , and $\gamma\geq 0$ , consider

$$ V_{\mathrm{GD}}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma):=r(\alpha-1-\ln\alpha)+r\beta+r\gamma. $$

Defining $x:=[\alpha,\beta,\gamma]^{\top}$ , $e_{1}:=[1,0,0]^{\top}$ , $\hat{k}:=\hat{K}e_{1}$ , a direct differentiation along the GD flow gives

$$ \displaystyle\dot{V}_{\mathrm{GD}}=r\left(1-\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)\dot{\alpha}+r\dot{\beta}+r\dot{\gamma} \displaystyle=4(x-e_{1})^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(r,r,r)\,(\hat{k}-\hat{K}x) \displaystyle=-4(x-e_{1})^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(r,r,r)\hat{K}(x-e_{1})\leq 0. $$

Thus $V_{\mathrm{GD}}$ is a smooth Lyapunov function for the GD continuous-time dynamics, and its decay is governed by a quadratic dissipation mechanism around the equilibrium $x=e_{1}$ , under the corresponding positivity assumptions on the above quadratic form.

This provides a useful conceptual contrast with the Muon dynamics. For GD, the evolution is compatible with a smooth energy landscape and a correspondingly smooth dissipation law. By contrast, the sign-based Muon update is intrinsically nonsmooth, and the quantity (40) does not play the role of a comparably smooth Lyapunov function. This helps explain why GD typically admits cleaner convergence behavior, whereas Muon more naturally exhibits switching effects and $O(\eta)$ -scale residual oscillations under a constant step size.

#### Proposition A.17 (GD river progress after hill reduction).

Assume that there exist $N_{\rm GD}\geq 0$ and $R_{\rm GD}>0$ such that $H_{k}\leq R_{\rm GD}^{2}\eta^{2}$ for all $k\geq N_{\rm GD}$ . In particular, the hill forcing $\psi_{k}$ is of order $O(\eta)$ for all $k\geq N_{\rm GD}$ . Suppose further that $\eta\leq\frac{1}{6\overline{\alpha}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}$ , and that $\eta$ is sufficiently small so that for all $k\geq N_{\rm GD}$ ,

$$ |\theta_{k}|\geq\max\left\{\frac{2(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c})^{1/2}}{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}},\sqrt{\frac{\Gamma_{\rm GD}}{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}}\right\}R_{\rm GD}\eta,\qquad\Gamma_{\rm GD}\gg 1. $$

Then the river variable $\theta_{k}$ contracts geometrically:

$$ |\theta_{k+1}|\leq(1-2\underline{\alpha}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\eta)|\theta_{k}|. $$

#### Proof.

By (29), we have $\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}=\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}$ . Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the $\hat{D}^{-1}$ -inner product yields

$$ |\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}|\leq\bigl(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\bigr)^{1/2}\bigl(\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}\bigr)^{1/2}=\bigl(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\bigr)^{1/2}\sqrt{H_{k}}. $$

Using $H_{k}\leq R_{\rm GD}^{2}\eta^{2}$ , we obtain $|\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}|\leq(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c})^{1/2}R_{\rm GD}\eta$ . If (35) holds, then

$$ |\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}|\leq\frac{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}{2}|\theta_{k}|\qquad\text{and}\qquad E_{k}=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}^{2}\geq\Gamma_{\rm GD}R_{\rm GD}^{2}\eta^{2}\gg H_{k}. $$

Consequently, the iterate is in a river-dominant phase, $\phi_{k}$ has the same sign as $\theta_{k}$ , and

$$ \frac{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}{2}|\theta_{k}|\leq|\phi_{k}|\leq\frac{3\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}{2}|\theta_{k}|. $$

Recall that the GD river update is $\theta_{k+1}=\theta_{k}-4\eta(1+\theta_{k})\phi_{k}$ . Using $1+\theta_{k}\geq\underline{\alpha}$ and the lower bound in (37), the update decreases $|\theta_{k}|$ by at least $2\underline{\alpha}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\eta|\theta_{k}|$ , provided that no overshoot occurs. To preclude overshoot, we use the upper bound in (37) and $\eta\leq\frac{1}{6\overline{\alpha}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}$ to obtain

$$ 4\eta(1+\theta_{k})|\phi_{k}|\leq 6\eta\overline{\alpha}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|\leq|\theta_{k}|. $$

Hence overshoot does not occur, and (36) follows. ∎

#### Remark A.18.

Proposition A.17 shows that once the hill forcing $\psi_{k}$ is reduced to order $O(\eta)$ (e.g., via (32)) and river energy dominates hill energy, the GD river variable $\theta_{k}$ contracts geometrically according to (36) until it reaches an $O(\eta)$ -neighborhood of the river equilibrium $\theta=0$ . Consequently, the number of GD iterations required to reduce $|\theta_{k}|$ from a constant scale to an $O(\eta)$ scale is

$$ O\!\left(\frac{1}{\eta}\log\frac{1}{\eta}\right). $$

Moreover, in practice GD may drive the hill forcing $\psi_{k}$ below the $O(\eta)$ level (i.e., achieve higher accuracy), whereas the corresponding simplified Muon analysis typically guarantees only an $O(\eta)$ -level transient bound. We therefore focus on the $O(\eta)$ regime to enable a like-for-like comparison with simplified Muon.

#### A.3.3 Simplified Muon Reduced Dynamics

The reduced Muon iteration follows readily from applying an Euler discretization to Lemma A.4:

$$ \begin{cases}\theta_{k+1}=\theta_{k}-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k},\qquad s_{k}\in\mathtt{sign}(\phi_{k}),\\
\omega_{k+1}=\omega_{k}-2\eta\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k},\qquad t_{k}\in\mathtt{sign}(\psi_{k}).\end{cases} $$

#### Proposition A.19 (Positivity preservation for reduced Muon).

Assume that $\eta>0$ is sufficiently small such that, for all $k$ ,

$$ 1+\theta_{k}>4\eta^{2},\qquad\omega_{k}\succ 4\eta^{2}\begin{bmatrix}1\\
1\end{bmatrix}. $$

Then, for any choices $s_{k}\in\mathtt{Sign}(\phi_{k})$ and $t_{k}\in\mathtt{Sign}(\psi_{k})$ , it holds that

$$ 1+\theta_{k+1}>0,\qquad\omega_{k+1}\succ 0. $$

#### Proof.

Since $s_{k}\in[-1,1]$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle 1+\theta_{k+1}=1+\theta_{k}-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}=\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}(\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}-2\eta s_{k})\geq\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}(\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}-2\eta)>0. $$

Similarly, for each $i\in\{1,2\}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle(\omega_{k+1})_{i}=(\omega_{k})_{i}-2\eta\sqrt{(\omega_{k})_{i}}\,(t_{k})_{i}=\sqrt{(\omega_{k})_{i}}\left[\sqrt{(\omega_{k})_{i}}-2\eta(t_{k})_{i}\right]\geq\sqrt{(\omega_{k})_{i}}\left[\sqrt{(\omega_{k})_{i}}-2\eta\right]>0. $$

This completes the proof. ∎

#### Proposition A.20 (Hill-energy estimate for reduced Muon).

Assume that the Muon orbit remains in the compact box $K_{\underline{\alpha},\overline{\alpha},\underline{\omega},\overline{\omega}}$ . Define the constants $B_{0}:=\sqrt{\underline{\omega}\mu}-\sqrt{\overline{\alpha}}\,(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c})^{1/2}$ and $B_{1}:=8\overline{\alpha}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+16\nu\overline{\omega}$ . Then

$$ H_{k+1}\leq H_{k}-4B_{0}\eta\sqrt{H_{k}}+B_{1}\eta^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

By definition, $\psi_{k+1}=\hat{c}\theta_{k+1}+\hat{D}\omega_{k+1}$ . Using 38, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\psi_{k+1} \displaystyle=\hat{c}\left[\theta_{k}-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}\right]+\hat{D}\left[\omega_{k}-2\eta\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\right] \displaystyle=\psi_{k}-2\eta\left[\hat{c}\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}+\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\right]. $$

Let $r_{k}:=\hat{c}\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}+\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}$ . Then $\psi_{k+1}=\psi_{k}-2\eta r_{k}$ , and hence

$$ H_{k+1}-H_{k}=-4\eta\,\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}+4\eta^{2}r_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}. $$

For the linear term, we can write

$$ \displaystyle\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}=\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+\psi_{k}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k} \displaystyle= \displaystyle\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+\sum_{i=1}^{2}\sqrt{(\omega_{k})_{i}}\,|(\psi_{k})_{i}|\geq-\sqrt{\overline{\alpha}}\bigl(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\bigr)^{1/2}\sqrt{H_{k}}+\sqrt{\underline{\omega}}\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}. $$

Since $\|\psi_{k}\|_{2}^{2}\geq\mu H_{k}$ , it follows that $\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}\geq B_{0}\sqrt{H_{k}}$ .

For the quadratic term, using $(u+v)^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}(u+v)\leq 2u^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}u+2v^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}v$ , we obtain

$$ \displaystyle r_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}=\left[\hat{c}\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}+\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\right]^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\left[\hat{c}\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}+\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle 2\bigl(\hat{c}\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}\bigr)^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\bigl(\hat{c}\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,s_{k}\bigr)+2\bigl(\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\bigr)^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\bigl(\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\bigr) \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2(1+\theta_{k})s_{k}^{2}\,\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+2\,t_{k}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}\hat{D}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\leq 2\overline{\alpha}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+2\nu\|\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k})^{1/2}t_{k}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\overline{\alpha}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+2\nu\sum_{i=1}^{2}(\omega_{k})_{i}(t_{k})_{i}^{2}\leq 2\overline{\alpha}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}+4\nu\overline{\omega}. $$

Multiplying by $4\eta^{2}$ yields

$$ 4\eta^{2}r_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}r_{k}\leq 8\overline{\alpha}\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\,\eta^{2}+16\nu\overline{\omega}\,\eta^{2}=B_{1}\eta^{2}. $$

Combining the bounds on the linear and quadratic terms gives (39). ∎

#### Corollary A.21 (Eventual $O(\eta)$ hill tube for reduced Muon).

Under the assumptions of the preceding proposition, define

$$ R_{\rm Muon}:=\max\left\{\frac{B_{1}}{2B_{0}},\sqrt{B_{1}}\right\}. $$

If $B_{0}>0$ and $\sqrt{H_{k}}\geq R_{\rm Muon}\eta$ , then

$$ H_{k+1}\leq H_{k}-B_{1}\eta^{2}. $$

Moreover, if $H_{k}\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ , then $H_{k+1}\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ . Consequently, the reduced Muon orbit enters and thereafter remains in the $O(\eta)$ hill tube, i.e., there exists $N_{\rm Muon}$ such that, for all $k\geq N_{\rm Muon}$ ,

$$ \|\psi_{k}\|_{2}\leq\sqrt{\nu}R_{\rm Muon}\eta. $$

#### Proof.

From (39), we have $H_{k+1}\leq H_{k}-4B_{0}\eta\sqrt{H_{k}}+B_{1}\eta^{2}$ .

If $B_{0}>0$ and $\sqrt{H_{k}}\geq R_{\rm Muon}\eta$ , then $R_{\rm Muon}\geq B_{1}/(2B_{0})$ implies

$$ 4B_{0}\eta\sqrt{H_{k}}\geq 2B_{1}\eta^{2}, $$

and therefore $H_{k+1}\leq H_{k}-B_{1}\eta^{2}$ .

To prove invariance of the tube, suppose $H_{k}\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ and consider

$$ f(y)=y-4B_{0}\eta\sqrt{y}+B_{1}\eta^{2}. $$

This function is concave on $[0,\infty)$ , hence it attains its maximum over $[0,R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}]$ at an endpoint. Using $R_{\rm Muon}\geq\sqrt{B_{1}}$ and $R_{\rm Muon}\geq B_{1}/(2B_{0})$ , one can check that $f(R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2})\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ and $f(0)\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ , which yields $H_{k+1}\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ . Thus, the tube is forward invariant.

Finally, outside the tube the energy decreases by at least $B_{1}\eta^{2}$ per step, which implies a finite hitting-time bound with

$$ N_{\rm Muon}=\left\lceil\frac{\max\{H_{0}-R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2},0\}}{B_{1}\eta^{2}}\right\rceil. $$

The proof is complete. ∎

#### Remark A.22 (A Lyapunov perspective on Simplified Muon).

The conclusion of Corollary A.21 depends essentially on the sign of $B_{0}$ . If $B_{0}<0$ , then Proposition A.20 yields

$$ H_{k+1}\leq H_{k}+4|B_{0}|\eta\sqrt{H_{k}}+B_{1}\eta^{2}, $$

which no longer implies a dissipative drift for the reduced hill energy $H_{k}$ . This is consistent with the optimization intuition behind Muon: sign-based dynamics can exhibit nonsmooth switching and transient oscillations in the river-valley coordinates, even when the full dynamics remain energy-dissipative. Writing $x=[\alpha,\beta,\gamma]^{\top}$ , and let $\hat{k}$ denote the first column of $\hat{K}$ . The Muon flow admits the Filippov signum form

$$ \dot{x}\in 2\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{x})\,\mathtt{Sign}(\hat{k}-\hat{K}x)=-2\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{x})\,\mathtt{Sign}\!\bigl(\hat{K}(x-e_{1})\bigr), $$

A natural Lyapunov candidate is the $\ell_{1}$ -potential of the residual,

$$ V_{\rm Muon}(x):=\|\hat{K}(x-e_{1})\|_{1}. $$

Since $V_{\rm Muon}$ is convex and locally Lipschitz, its Clarke generalized gradient coincides with its convex subdifferential, and

$$ \partial V_{\rm Muon}(x)=\hat{K}^{\top}\,\mathtt{Sign}\!\bigl(\hat{K}(x-e_{1})\bigr). $$

Hence, for almost every $t$ , one may choose $\sigma(t)\in\mathtt{Sign}(\hat{K}(x(t)-e_{1}))$ such that

$$ \dot{x}(t)=-2\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{x(t)})\,\sigma(t),\qquad g(t):=\hat{K}^{\top}\sigma(t)\in\partial V_{\rm Muon}(x(t)). $$

By the Clarke chain rule for locally Lipschitz Lyapunov functions along differential inclusions,

$$ \dot{V}_{\rm Muon}\bigl(x(t);\dot{x}(t)\bigr)\leq g(t)^{\top}\dot{x}(t)=-2\,\sigma(t)^{\top}\hat{K}\,\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{x(t)})\,\sigma(t)\leq 0\qquad\text{for a.e. }t, $$

Therefore, although the reduced hill energy $H_{k}$ need not be monotone when $B_{0}<0$ , the full Muon dynamics still admit a natural nonincreasing energy functional. In this sense, the condition $B_{0}>0$ should be viewed as a technical assumption that excludes hill-direction excitation at the level of the reduced recursion, thereby yielding a clean one-step contraction estimate.

#### Proposition A.23 (Muon river progress after hill reduction).

Assume there exist $N_{\rm Muon}\geq 0$ and $R_{\rm Muon}>0$ such that $H_{k}\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ for all $k\geq N_{\rm Muon}$ . In particular, the hill forcing $\psi_{k}$ is $O(\eta)$ for all $k\geq N_{\rm Muon}$ . Suppose further that $\eta$ is sufficiently small so that, for all $k\geq N_{\rm Muon}$ ,

$$ |\theta_{k}|\geq\max\left\{\frac{2\bigl(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\bigr)^{1/2}R_{\rm Muon}}{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}\eta,\,2\sqrt{\overline{\alpha}}\,\eta,\,\sqrt{\frac{\Gamma_{\rm Muon}}{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}}R_{\rm Muon}\eta\right\},\qquad\Gamma_{\rm Muon}\gg 1. $$

Then the river variable $\theta_{k}$ contracts linearly in the sense that

$$ |\theta_{k+1}|\leq|\theta_{k}|-2\sqrt{\underline{\alpha}}\,\eta. $$

#### Proof.

By (29), we have $\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}=\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}$ . Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the $\hat{D}^{-1}$ -inner product yields

$$ |\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}|\leq\bigl(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\bigr)^{1/2}\bigl(\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}\bigr)^{1/2}=\bigl(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\bigr)^{1/2}\sqrt{H_{k}}. $$

For $k\geq N_{\rm Muon}$ , Corollary A.21 gives $H_{k}\leq R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}$ , and hence

$$ |\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}|\leq\bigl(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}\bigr)^{1/2}R_{\rm Muon}\eta. $$

If (41) holds, then

$$ |\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}|\leq\frac{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}{2}|\theta_{k}|\qquad\text{and}\qquad E_{k}=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}^{2}\geq\Gamma_{\rm Muon}R_{\rm Muon}^{2}\eta^{2}\gg H_{k}. $$

Consequently, the iterate is in a river-dominant phase, $\phi_{k}$ has the same sign as $\theta_{k}$ , and $|\phi_{k}|\geq\frac{\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}{2}|\theta_{k}|$ .

Moreover, the second term in (41) implies (41) gives $|\theta_{k}|\geq 2\sqrt{\overline{\alpha}}\,\eta$ . Since $1+\theta_{k}\leq\overline{\alpha}$ , we obtain $2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\leq 2\eta\sqrt{\overline{\alpha}}\leq|\theta_{k}|$ . Thus, the river update does not cross the origin. Using the river recursion together with $\mathtt{sign}(\phi_{k})=\mathtt{sign}(\theta_{k})$ , we obtain

$$ |\theta_{k+1}|=\left|\theta_{k}-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,\mathtt{sign}(\phi_{k})\right|=\left|\theta_{k}-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,\mathtt{sign}(\theta_{k})\right|=|\theta_{k}|-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}. $$

Finally, since $1+\theta_{k}\geq\underline{\alpha}$ , (42) follows. ∎

#### Remark A.24.

Proposition A.23 shows that once the hill forcing $\psi_{k}$ is reduced to order $O(\eta)$ (e.g., via (39)) and river energy dominates hill energy, the Muon river variable $\theta_{k}$ contracts linearly according to (42) until it reaches an $O(\eta)$ -neighborhood of the river equilibrium $\theta=0$ . Consequently, the number of Muon iterations required to reduce $|\theta_{k}|$ from a constant scale to an $O(\eta)$ scale is

$$ O\!\left(\frac{1}{\eta}\right). $$

We emphasize that this analysis under a constant step size typically yields at best an $O(\eta)$ -accuracy guarantee. This behavior is consistent with the sign-based Muon update: the induced nonsmooth switching can produce persistent $O(\eta)$ -scale oscillations in both the hill and river directions. Thus, one should not generally expect the discrete iterates to converge exactly to the equilibrium.

#### Proposition A.25 (Late-stage behavior in a relative river tube).

Assume that the river curvature $\hat{a}_{\rm eff}>0$ . Fix a constant $\bar{\rho}\in(0,1)$ . Suppose that, on the time interval under consideration, the iterates satisfy $0<\underline{\alpha}\leq 1+\theta_{k}\leq\overline{\alpha}$ and remain in the following relative river tube:

$$ \sqrt{\bar{q}H_{k}}\leq\bar{\rho}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|. $$

Then the following statements hold.

(i) Vanilla GD naturally refines. If the step size satisfies $0<\eta\leq\min\{\frac{1}{4\overline{\alpha}(1+\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}},\frac{1}{4\underline{\alpha}(1-\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}\}$ , then vanilla GD can refine the river variable from $O(\eta)$ to any target accuracy $\varepsilon\ll\eta$ .

(ii) Fixed-step simplified Muon overshoots near the river equilibrium. Under the relative tube condition, if $0<|\theta_{k}|<\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}$ , then the river energy increases after one Muon step: $E_{k+1}>E_{k}$ .

#### Proof.

Recall that (29) is $\phi_{k}=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}+\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}$ . By Cauchy-Schwarz in the $\hat{D}^{-1}$ -inner product,

$$ |\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}|^{2}\leq(\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c})(\psi_{k}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k})=\bar{q}H_{k}. $$

Therefore, $\left|\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}\right|\leq\sqrt{\bar{q}H_{k}}$ . Using the relative tube condition (12), we obtain

$$ \left|\phi_{k}-\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}\right|\leq\bar{\rho}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|. $$

Since $\bar{\rho}\in(0,1)$ and $\hat{a}_{\rm eff}>0$ , this implies that $\phi_{k}$ has the same sign as $\theta_{k}$ whenever $\theta_{k}\neq 0$ . It also implies the two-sided bound

$$ (1-\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|\leq|\phi_{k}|\leq(1+\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|. $$

We now prove the vanilla GD refinement statement. The vanilla GD river iteration is

$$ \theta_{k+1}=\theta_{k}-4\eta(1+\theta_{k})\phi_{k}. $$

Since $\phi_{k}$ and $\theta_{k}$ have the same sign, the update moves toward zero in the river coordinate. Using the upper bound in (43) and $1+\theta_{k}\leq\overline{\alpha}$ ,

$$ 4\eta(1+\theta_{k})|\phi_{k}|\leq 4\eta\overline{\alpha}(1+\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|. $$

By the step-size condition $0<\eta\leq\frac{1}{4\overline{\alpha}(1+\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}$ , we have $4\eta(1+\theta_{k})|\phi_{k}|\leq|\theta_{k}|$ . Hence GD does not overshoot zero, and

$$ |\theta_{k+1}|\leq|\theta_{k}|-4\eta\underline{\alpha}(1-\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|=\left[1-4\eta\underline{\alpha}(1-\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\right]|\theta_{k}|. $$

Iterating the contraction gives

$$ |\theta_{k_{0}+t}|\leq\left[1-4\eta\underline{\alpha}(1-\bar{\rho})\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\right]^{t}|\theta_{k_{0}}|\leq\varepsilon. $$

Thus it is enough to take

$$ t\geq\frac{1}{4\eta\underline{\alpha}(1-\rho)\hat{a}_{\rm eff}}\log\frac{|\theta_{k_{0}}|}{\varepsilon}. $$

We next prove the simplified Muon overshoot statement. Under the relative tube condition, the simplified Muon river iteration becomes

$$ \displaystyle\theta_{k+1}=\theta_{k}-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,\mathtt{sign}(\phi_{k})=\theta_{k}-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\,\mathtt{sign}(\theta_{k})=\mathtt{sign}(\theta_{k})\left(|\theta_{k}|-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}\right). $$

$\theta_{k+1}$ has the opposite sign from $\theta_{k}$ if $|\theta_{k}|<2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}$ . This proves $\theta_{k}\theta_{k+1}<0$ .

It remains to prove the one-step river-energy increase. Since $E_{k}=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}^{2}$ , we only need to compare $|\theta_{k+1}|$ and $|\theta_{k}|$ . We already have

$$ |\theta_{k+1}|=||\theta_{k}|-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}|. $$

If $0<|\theta_{k}|<\frac{2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}}{2}$ , then

$$ |\theta_{k+1}|=||\theta_{k}|-2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}|=2\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}-|\theta_{k}|>|\theta_{k}|. $$

Therefore

$$ E_{k+1}=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k+1}^{2}>\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}^{2}=E_{k}. $$

Finally, note that as $\theta_{k}\to 0$ , the condition $0<|\theta_{k}|<\eta\sqrt{1+\theta_{k}}$ must eventually hold in the late-stage refinement regime when the step size is fixed; thus overshooting occurs inevitably near equilibrium. This completes the proof. ∎

#### Remark A.26 (Why the relative river-tube condition is natural).

The relative river-tube condition

$$ \sqrt{\bar{q}H_{k}}\leq\bar{\rho}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|,\qquad 0<\bar{\rho}<1, $$

should be interpreted as the late-stage version of river dominance. Indeed, the river force admits the decomposition $\phi_{k}=\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}+\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k},$ and the perturbation caused by the residual hill force satisfies

$$ \bigl|\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\psi_{k}\bigr|\leq\sqrt{\bar{q}H_{k}},\qquad\bar{q}:=\hat{c}^{\top}\hat{D}^{-1}\hat{c}. $$

Therefore the relative tube condition is exactly the requirement that the hill-induced perturbation of the river force is at most a $\rho$ -fraction of the intrinsic river force $\hat{a}_{\rm eff}\theta_{k}$ . Equivalently, it guarantees that $\phi_{k}$ has the same sign as $\theta_{k}$ , so the dynamics can still be interpreted as refinement along the river.

This condition is automatic on the exact reduced river $\psi_{k}=0$ , and it also holds in any sufficiently thin $O(|\theta_{k}|)$ -neighborhood (now $\theta_{k}$ enters an $O(\eta)$ neighborhood of equilibrium) of that river:

$$ H_{k}\leq\frac{\bar{\rho}^{2}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}^{2}}{\bar{q}}\,\theta_{k}^{2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\sqrt{\bar{q}H_{k}}\leq\bar{\rho}\hat{a}_{\rm eff}|\theta_{k}|. $$

Thus the condition is not an additional geometric object; it is a quantitative way of saying that, even in the coupled PSD case, the iterate is close enough to the tilted river for the remaining force to be river-dominated.

## Appendix B Additional Details for Section 4

### B.1 Spectral-River Geometry

In this section, we study the optimization of a general objective function $\mathcal{F}(X):\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ with the goal of finding a critical point $X^{\star}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ , i.e., $\nabla\mathcal{F}(X^{\star})=0$ . We assume that the target matrix $X^{\star}$ (also called the ground truth) admits the singular value decomposition (SVD)

$$ X^{\star}=U_{\star}\Sigma_{\star}V_{\star}^{\top},\qquad U_{\star}^{\top}U_{\star}=I_{n},\qquad V_{\star}^{\top}V_{\star}=I_{n},\qquad\Sigma_{\star}=\mathtt{Diag}(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{n}), $$

with $\sigma_{i}>0$ . The rank-deficient case follows by replacing $n$ with the signal rank $r$ and restricting attention to the corresponding signal block. Therefore, we focus on the square case for simplicity, though the optimization variable $X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ can be generalized to a rectangular matrix.

#### Definition B.1 (Spectral embedding and spectral river).

We define the spectral embedding $\mathcal{B}:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ by $\mathcal{B}(x):=U_{\star}\mathtt{Diag}(x)V_{\star}^{\top}$ for any $x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ . The spectral river through $X^{\star}$ is the affine set

$$ \mathcal{R}^{\star}:=\{X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x)\,\mid\,x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}. $$

Since $X^{\star}=\mathcal{B}(\sigma)$ with $\sigma:=[\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{n}]^{\top}$ , any $Y\in\mathcal{R}^{\star}$ can be written as $Y=\mathcal{B}(y)$ for some $y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ , equivalently $Y=U_{\star}\mathtt{Diag}(y)V_{\star}^{\top}$ . Therefore, any point $Y$ on the river shares the left/right singular vector subspaces $(U_{\star},V_{\star})$ with $X^{\star}$ ; only the singular-value magnitudes vary along the river. Moreover, $\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{1})=U_{\star}V_{\star}^{\top}$ and $\|\mathcal{B}(x)\|_{F}=\|x\|_{2}$ .

#### Definition B.2 (River-restricted objective).

We define the objective restricted to the spectral river (i.e., the pullback of $\mathcal{F}$ under the map $x\mapsto X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x)$ ) as

$$ f(x):=\mathcal{F}\bigl(X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x)\bigr)-\mathcal{F}(X^{\star}),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}. $$

#### Definition B.3 (Positive chamber).

We define the positive chamber of the spectral river as

$$ \mathcal{R}^{\star}_{+}:=\{X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x)\,\mid\,\sigma+x\succ\mathbf{0}\}=\{U_{\star}\mathtt{Diag}(y)V_{\star}^{\top}\,\mid\,y\succ\mathbf{0}\}. $$

Within this chamber, the polar factor is constant and equals $\mathtt{msign}(Y)=\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{1})$ for all $Y\in\mathcal{R}^{\star}_{+}$ . Moreover, if some entries of $y$ are negative (so that $Y=U_{\star}\mathtt{Diag}(y)V_{\star}^{\top}$ has mixed signs), then the polar factor becomes $U_{\star}\mathtt{Diag}(\mathtt{sign}(y))V_{\star}^{\top}$ .

#### Definition B.4 (Orthogonal basis and projection operator).

For each $i=1,\cdots,n$ , define the basis matrices for the river direction space $\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\ldots,B_{n}\}$ using the $i$ -th standard basis vector $e_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ :

$$ B_{i}:=U_{\star}e_{i}e_{i}^{\top}V_{\star}^{\top}. $$

These matrices form an orthonormal set under the Frobenius inner product, i.e., $\langle B_{i},B_{j}\rangle=\delta_{ij}$ . Consequently, $\mathcal{B}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}B_{i}$ and $\langle\mathcal{B}(x),\mathcal{B}(y)\rangle=x^{\top}y$ . Moreover, for any $Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ , the (Frobenius) orthogonal projection onto $\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}$ is

$$ \mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(Y)=\sum\nolimits_{i=1}^{n}\left\langle B_{i},Y\right\rangle B_{i}=U_{\star}\mathtt{Diag}\bigl(\mathtt{diag}(U_{\star}^{\top}YV_{\star})\bigr)V_{\star}^{\top}. $$

#### Definition B.5 (Spectral-river tube).

Fix a scale $\delta>0$ . Define the $\delta$ -tube around the spectral river $\mathcal{R}^{\star}:=X^{\star}+\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}$ by

$$ \mathcal{T}_{\delta}(\mathcal{R}^{\star}):=\left\{X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\,\middle|\,\mathtt{dist}_{F}\!\left(X,\mathcal{R}^{\star}\right)\leq\delta\right\}, $$

where $\mathtt{dist}_{F}(X,\mathcal{R}^{\star}):=\inf_{Y\in\mathcal{R}^{\star}}\|X-Y\|_{F}$ . Equivalently, each $X$ admits a unique orthogonal decomposition

$$ X=X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x)+E^{\perp},\qquad E^{\perp}\in\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}^{\perp}, $$

and $X\in\mathcal{T}_{\delta}(\mathcal{R}^{\star})$ if and only if $\|E^{\perp}\|_{F}\leq\delta$ .

#### Definition B.6 (Hill component and river-dominance).

For any $Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ , we define its hill component as $\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(Y)$ , where $\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(\cdot)$ denotes the Frobenius-orthogonal projections onto $\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}$ ’s orthogonal complement, i.e., $\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}^{\perp}$ . We say that $Y$ is river-dominated if its hill component is small relative to its river component.

#### Lemma B.7 (Hessian projection).

Let $\mathcal{H}_{\star}:=\nabla^{2}\mathcal{F}(X^{\star})$ , viewed as a linear operator acting on matrices. If the river residual is $\mathcal{B}(x)$ , then its Hessian image projected back onto the river direction space satisfies

$$ \displaystyle\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}\bigl(\mathcal{H}_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(x)]\bigr)=\sum\nolimits_{i=1}^{n}\left\langle B_{i},\mathcal{H}_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(x)]\right\rangle B_{i}=\sum\nolimits_{i=1}^{n}\left\langle B_{i},\sum\nolimits_{j=1}^{n}x_{j}\mathcal{H}_{\star}[B_{j}]\right\rangle B_{i} \displaystyle= \displaystyle\sum\nolimits_{i=1}^{n}\left(\sum\nolimits_{j=1}^{n}x_{j}\left\langle B_{i},\mathcal{H}_{\star}[B_{j}]\right\rangle\right)B_{i}=\sum\nolimits_{i=1}^{n}\left(\sum\nolimits_{j=1}^{n}K_{ij}x_{j}\right)B_{i}=\mathcal{R}(Kx), $$

where $K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is the coordinate matrix of the projected Hessian action in the basis $\{B_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}$ , defined by

$$ K_{ij}:=\left\langle B_{i},\mathcal{H}_{\star}[B_{j}]\right\rangle. $$

If $\mathcal{F}$ is twice continuously differentiable, then $\mathcal{H}_{\star}$ is self-adjoint w.r.t. the Frobenius inner product, hence $K$ is symmetric. Moreover, near the critical point $X^{\star}$ (as $a\to 0$ ), a second-order expansion yields

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X^{\star}+a\mathcal{B}(x))=a\,\mathcal{H}_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(x)]+O(a^{2}). $$

If the off-river component of $\mathcal{H}_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(x)]$ is negligible so that $\mathcal{H}_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(x)]\approx\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}\bigl(\mathcal{H}_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(x)]\bigr)=\mathcal{B}(Kx)$ and $Kx\succ\mathbf{0}$ , then the resulting gradient direction lies in the positive chamber, and hence $\mathtt{msign}(\mathcal{B}(Kx))=\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{1})$ . Note that Muon observes $\mathcal{H}_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(x)]$ rather than $\mathcal{B}(x)$ itself; however, in later analysis we will assume that the river component dominates.

### B.2 Early-Stage: When Muon Accelerates River Progress

This subsection establishes an early-stage regime in which Muon accelerates progress along the spectral river. Our goal is to isolate conditions under which the effective curvature restricted to the river is substantially smaller than the ambient curvature in the full matrix space. In such a regime, a Muon step that is aligned with the river geometry can admit a provably larger decrease than a conservative gradient step. We adopt the following local smoothness assumption.

#### Assumption B.8 (Local smoothness separation for $\mathcal{F}$ and $f$ ).

Fix a neighborhood of interest around the current iterate(s). There exist constants $L_{\rm full},L_{\rm riv}>0$ with $L_{\rm riv}\ll L_{\rm full}$ such that, for all $X$ in this neighborhood and all sufficiently small perturbations $\Delta X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ ,

$$ \|\nabla\mathcal{F}(X+\Delta X)-\nabla\mathcal{F}(X)\|_{F}\leq L_{\rm full}\,\|\Delta X\|_{F}. $$

Moreover, for all $x$ in the corresponding river neighborhood and all sufficiently small $\Delta x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ , the river-restricted objective $f$ satisfies

$$ f(x+\Delta x)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),\Delta x\rangle+\frac{L_{\rm riv}}{2}\|\Delta x\|_{2}^{2}. $$

Here (52) is the standard Lipschitz continuity of $\nabla\mathcal{F}$ (in Frobenius norm), while (53) is the usual quadratic upper bound (descent lemma [59]) for $f$ , which is implied by $\nabla f$ being $L_{\rm riv}$ -Lipschitz on the neighborhood.

Because $L_{\rm full}$ controls smoothness in all directions, it can be dominated by high-curvature components (e.g., “spike” directions). In contrast, $L_{\rm riv}$ quantifies curvature only along the signal-aligned, singular-value directions parametrized by the river. This separation generalizes the mixed-spiked MS dynamics developed in this paper: river coefficients may remain well-conditioned even when transverse “hill” directions are stiff and therefore force conservative gradient steps. Consequently, once the iterates lie on or near the river, the effective constant $L_{\rm riv}$ governing Muon’s motion can be substantially smaller than the global constant $L_{\rm full}$ that limits vanilla gradient methods.

#### Early-stage: a one-step comparison.

We formalize a simple one-step manifestation of the early-stage speedup. Fix a point on the spectral river

$$ X_{0}\;=\;X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x_{0}). $$

(Here “ $0$ ” indicates the point at which we start the analysis, not necessarily the initialization of the algorithm.) We compare the certified one-step decrease obtained by a momentum-Muon step aligned with the river geometry versus a conservative gradient step whose step size is limited by the ambient smoothness.

- • One-step momentum-Muon (ambient form). Given a stored momentum matrix $M_{0}^{\rm Muon}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and momentum parameter $\xi\geq 0$ , define

$$ M_{1}^{\rm Muon}=\xi M_{0}^{\rm Muon}+\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0}),\qquad X_{1}^{\rm Muon}=X_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\,\mathtt{msign}(M_{1}^{\rm Muon}). $$

- • One-step vanilla gradient descent (ambient form). With step size $\eta^{\rm GD}>0$ ,

$$ X_{1}^{\rm GD}\;=\;X_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0}). $$

The key technical simplification is that, under a (local) gradient-invariance condition, the ambient gradients and momenta can be represented in the river coordinates, allowing us to reduce the comparison from $\mathcal{F}$ on matrices to $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ .

#### Lemma B.9 (River reduction under gradient invariance).

Suppose the Muon momentum is river-aligned in the sense that

$$ M_{0}^{\rm Muon}=\mathcal{B}(m_{0})\quad\text{and}\quad M_{1}^{\rm Muon}=\mathcal{B}(m_{1})\qquad\text{for some }m_{0},m_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}. $$

Assume moreover that the river is gradient-invariant at $X_{0}=X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x_{0})$ , namely

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=\mathcal{B}\bigl(\nabla f(x_{0})\bigr). $$

Then the momentum update in the ambient space is equivalent to the river-coordinate update

$$ M_{1}^{\rm Muon}=\xi M_{0}^{\rm Muon}+\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad m_{1}=\xi m_{0}+\nabla f(x_{0}). $$

In particular, the corresponding sign directions satisfy $\mathtt{msign}(M_{1}^{\rm Muon})=\mathcal{B}(\mathtt{sign}(m_{1}))$ .

Furthermore, if $m_{0}$ is coordinate-wise sign-aligned with $\nabla f(x_{0})$ , then

$$ \langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle=\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{1}. $$

More generally, without requiring sign alignment, define

$$ \rho\;:=\;\frac{\langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle}{\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{1}}, $$

whenever $\nabla f(x_{0})\neq 0$ . Then $\rho\in(0,1]$ precisely captures the degree of sign agreement and yields

$$ \langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle\;\geq\;\rho\,\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{1}. $$

#### Proof.

The equivalence follows by substituting $M_{0}^{\rm Muon}=\mathcal{B}(m_{0})$ and (54) into Muon’s momentum update and using linearity of $\mathcal{B}$ . The statement about sign directions follows from the definition of $\mathtt{msign}(\cdot)$ and the coordinate-wise nature of $\mathtt{sign}(\cdot)$ . If $m_{0}$ and $\nabla f(x_{0})$ are coordinate-wise sign-aligned, then $m_{1}=\xi m_{0}+\nabla f(x_{0})$ has the same sign pattern as $\nabla f(x_{0})$ , hence $\langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle=\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{1}$ . (55) is immediate from the definition of $\rho$ . ∎

By Lemma B.9, it suffices to compare the following river-coordinate one-step updates:

- • One-step momentum-Muon (river form).

$$ m_{1}=\xi m_{0}+\nabla f(x_{0}),\qquad x_{1}^{\rm Muon}=x_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\,\mathtt{sign}(m_{1}). $$

- • One-step vanilla gradient descent (river form).

$$ x_{1}^{\rm GD}=x_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}\nabla f(x_{0}). $$

#### Theorem B.10 (Early-stage Muon acceleration along the spectral river (one-step analysis)).

Assume the local smoothness conditions in Assumption B.8 hold and that the gradient-invariance condition (54) holds at $x_{0}$ . Fix $\rho\in(0,1]$ as in (55), and assume $\nabla f(x_{0})\neq 0$ .

- • (Muon decrease along the sign direction.) Let $\eta^{\rm Muon}=\langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle/(L_{\rm riv}n)$ , then the one-step update $x_{1}^{\rm Muon}=x_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})$ satisfies

$$ f(x_{1}^{\rm Muon})\leq f(x_{0})-\frac{\langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle^{2}}{2L_{\rm riv}\,\|\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\|_{2}^{2}}\leq f(x_{0})-\frac{\rho^{2}\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{1}^{2}}{2L_{\rm riv}\,n}, $$

where we used $\|\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\|_{2}^{2}=n$ (assume no ties so that $\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\in\{\pm 1\}^{n}$ ) and (55).

- • (Conservative GD decrease under ambient step size.) With the conservative choice $\eta^{\rm GD}=1/L_{\rm full}$ , the GD update $x_{1}^{\rm GD}=x_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}\nabla f(x_{0})$ satisfies

$$ f(x_{1}^{\rm GD})\leq f(x_{0})-\frac{\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{2}^{2}}{2L_{\rm full}}, $$

whenever $L_{\rm full}\geq L_{\rm riv}$ .

Consequently, the certified Muon decrease is larger than the certified conservative GD decrease whenever

$$ \rho^{2}\frac{L_{\rm full}}{L_{\rm riv}}\cdot\frac{\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{1}^{2}}{n\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{2}^{2}}\;>\;1. $$

Equivalently, the certified speedup factor satisfies

$$ \frac{\textnormal{Muon decrease}}{\textnormal{GD decrease}}\geq\rho^{2}\frac{L_{\rm full}}{L_{\rm riv}}\cdot\frac{\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{1}^{2}}{n\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{2}^{2}}. $$

#### Proof.

For the momentum-Muon step, apply the descent lemma [59] for the $L_{\rm riv}$ -smooth function $f$ with direction $\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})$ :

$$ f(x_{0}-\eta\mathtt{sign}(m_{1}))\leq f(x_{0})-\eta\langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle+\frac{L_{\rm riv}}{2}\eta^{2}\|\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\|_{2}^{2}. $$

The right-hand side is minimized at $\eta=\langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle/(L_{\rm riv}\|\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\|_{2}^{2})$ , which yields

$$ f(x_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathtt{sign}(m_{1}))\leq f(x_{0})-\frac{\langle\nabla f(x_{0}),\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\rangle^{2}}{2L_{\rm riv}\|\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\|_{2}^{2}}. $$

Using $\|\mathtt{sign}(m_{1})\|_{2}^{2}=n$ together with (55) gives the claimed bound.

For gradient descent, apply the same descent lemma with direction $\nabla f(x_{0})$ and step size $\eta^{\rm GD}=1/L_{\rm full}$ :

$$ f\!\left(x_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}\nabla f(x_{0})\right)\leq f(x_{0})-\frac{1}{L_{\rm full}}\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{2}^{2}+\frac{L_{\rm riv}}{2L_{\rm full}^{2}}\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{2}^{2}. $$

If $L_{\rm full}\geq L_{\rm riv}$ , then the last two terms combine to $-\|\nabla f(x_{0})\|_{2}^{2}/(2L_{\rm full})$ , which completes the proof. ∎

#### Remark B.11 (When can $L_{\rm riv}\ll L_{\rm full}$ occur?).

The inequality $L_{\rm riv}\leq L_{\rm full}$ is natural: $L_{\rm riv}$ quantifies smoothness only along the river directions, while $L_{\rm full}$ controls smoothness over all ambient directions. A pronounced gap arises when the local Hessian is much flatter on the river than on its transverse complement. Concretely, with respect to the orthogonal decomposition $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{R}_{\star}\oplus\mathcal{R}_{\star}^{\perp}$ , if the Hessian admits an (approximately) block-structured form

$$ \nabla^{2}\mathcal{F}(X)\approx\begin{pmatrix}K_{\star}&K_{\circ}^{\top}\\
K_{\circ}&K_{\diamond}\end{pmatrix}, $$

where the cross-coupling is small (e.g., $\|K_{\circ}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is small, corresponds to “bulk”) and the transverse hill block is much stiffer than the river block (i.e., $\|K_{\diamond}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\gg\|K_{\star}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ , “spike” $\gg$ “signal”), then one expects

$$ L_{\rm riv}\approx\|K_{\star}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad L_{\rm full}\approx\|\nabla^{2}\mathcal{F}(X)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\approx\|K_{\diamond}\|_{\mathrm{op}}. $$

In this regime, conservative gradient steps are limited by high-curvature off-river (“hill”) directions, whereas Muon can exploit the milder geometry along the information-bearing spectral river.

### B.3 Late-Stage: When Muon Fails in River Refinement

We now turn to the late-stage regime, in which the iterate is already close to the optimum and the residual magnitude is small. In this regime, the spectral polar operator $\mathtt{msign}(\cdot)$ —which discards singular-value magnitudes by keeping only their signs—can become harmful. Intuitively, the same scale-invariance that helps Muon rapidly align with the river direction early on may prevent the algorithm from making progressively smaller, well-calibrated corrections near the solution. As a result, Muon can exhibit a coarse “quantized” motion that overshoots the minimizer, whereas a suitably small gradient(-momentum) step continues to refine.

The next subsection isolates this phenomenon in an exactly solvable quadratic model, where all statements can be proved without approximation.

#### B.3.1 A toy quadratic model: explicit overshoot under $\mathtt{msign}$

We strip away nonessential nonlinear effects and retain only a strictly quadratic geometry:

$$ \mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X):=\frac{1}{2}\left\lVert X-X^{\star}\right\rVert_{F}^{2},\qquad X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}. $$

For (56), one has

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X)=X-X^{\star},\qquad\nabla^{2}\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X)=I, $$

so the gradient is exactly the residual. In particular, at any river point $X=X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x)$ ,

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X)=\mathcal{B}(x), $$

hence the gradient-invariance property holds automatically (no additional assumption is needed).

The river-restricted objective induced by (56) is

$$ f_{\rm quad}(x):=\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}\!\left(X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x)\right)-\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X^{\star})=\frac{1}{2}\|\mathcal{B}(x)\|_{F}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\|x\|_{2}^{2}, $$

and therefore $\nabla f_{\rm quad}(x)=x$ and $\nabla^{2}f_{\rm quad}(x)=I_{n}$ .

#### Update rules (river form).

In this subsection we work directly in river coordinates, using (57). We consider a momentum-Muon update that moves along the sign direction ( $\mathtt{msign}$ becomes $\mathtt{sign}$ ):

$$ m_{t+1}^{\rm Muon}=\xi m_{t}^{\rm Muon}+x_{t}^{\rm Muon},\qquad x_{t+1}^{\rm Muon}=x_{t}^{\rm Muon}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\,\mathtt{sign}(m_{t+1}^{\rm Muon}), $$

and we compare it against a (heavy-ball style) momentum gradient method that uses the full momentum magnitude (i.e., a kind of momentum-GD):

$$ m_{t+1}^{\rm GD}=\xi m_{t}^{\rm GD}+x_{t}^{\rm GD},\qquad x_{t+1}^{\rm GD}=x_{t}^{\rm GD}-\eta^{\rm GD}m_{t+1}^{\rm GD}. $$

Both are initialized from the same $(x_{0},m_{0})$ .

#### Proposition B.12 (Exact quadratic separation: Muon overshoots while momentum GD refines).

Fix $\xi\geq 0$ and consider (56). Let $X_{0}=X^{\star}+a\,\mathcal{B}(x_{0})$ with $a\in(0,1)$ and $x_{0}\succ\mathbf{0}$ . Assume the stored momentum is river-aligned and small:

$$ M_{0}=\mathcal{B}(m_{0}),\qquad m_{0}\succ\mathbf{0},\qquad\|m_{0}\|_{2}\leq C_{m}\,a, $$

for some constant $C_{m}$ independent of $a$ . Define the coordinate average $\bar{x}_{0}:=\frac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}^{\top}x_{0}$ .

Choose a Muon step size of the form

$$ \eta^{\rm Muon}=(1+\varepsilon)\,a\,\bar{x}_{0},\qquad\text{for some }\varepsilon\in(0,1). $$

Assume moreover that the second Muon momentum remains in the positive chamber:

$$ \xi^{2}m_{0}+a\left[(1+\xi)x_{0}-(1+\varepsilon)\bar{x}_{0}\,\mathbf{1}\right]\succ\mathbf{0}. $$

Then the Muon iterates satisfy a strict two-step overshoot:

$$ \mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}\!\left(X_{1}^{\rm Muon}\right)<\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X_{0})<\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}\!\left(X_{2}^{\rm Muon}\right). $$

Moreover, there exists a constant $\eta_{0}>0$ , depending only on $(\xi,x_{0},C_{m})$ but not on $a$ , such that the momentum-GD iterates initialized from the same $(X_{0},M_{0})$ satisfy

$$ \mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}\!\left(X_{2}^{\rm GD}\right)<\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X_{0})\qquad\text{for all}\qquad 0<\eta^{\rm GD}\leq\eta_{0}. $$

In particular, since $\eta^{\rm Muon}=O(a)$ while $\eta_{0}=O(1)$ , we have $\eta^{\rm Muon}<\eta_{0}$ for all sufficiently small $a$ .

#### Proof.

Throughout the proof, we use the river objective (57), i.e., $f_{\rm quad}(x)=\frac{1}{2}\|x\|_{2}^{2}$ , and the identity $\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(x))-\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X^{\star})=f_{\rm quad}(x)$ . Thus it suffices to compare the squared norms of the corresponding river coordinates.

#### Step 1: Muon decreases at the first step.

At $X_{0}=X^{\star}+a\mathcal{B}(x_{0})$ we have $\nabla\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X_{0})=a\mathcal{B}(x_{0})$ , hence the first Muon momentum is

$$ M_{1}^{\rm Muon}=\xi M_{0}+\nabla\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X_{0})=\mathcal{B}(\xi m_{0}+ax_{0}). $$

Since $m_{0}\succ\mathbf{0}$ and $x_{0}\succ\mathbf{0}$ , we obtain $\xi m_{0}+ax_{0}\succ\mathbf{0}$ , and therefore $\mathtt{sign}(\xi m_{0}+ax_{0})=\mathbf{1}$ . Consequently, the first Muon iterate in river coordinates is

$$ x_{1}^{\rm Muon}=ax_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1}. $$

A direct expansion yields

$$ \displaystyle f_{\rm quad}(x_{1}^{\rm Muon})-f_{\rm quad}(ax_{0}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\|ax_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1}\|_{2}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\|ax_{0}\|_{2}^{2}=-\eta^{\rm Muon}\,a\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}x_{0}+\frac{(\eta^{\rm Muon})^{2}}{2}\,\|\mathbf{1}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle=-\eta^{\rm Muon}\,a\,n\bar{x}_{0}+\frac{(\eta^{\rm Muon})^{2}}{2}\,n=\frac{n}{2}\,\eta^{\rm Muon}\left(\eta^{\rm Muon}-2a\bar{x}_{0}\right). $$

With $\eta^{\rm Muon}=(1+\varepsilon)a\bar{x}_{0}$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ , we have $\eta^{\rm Muon}-2a\bar{x}_{0}=(\varepsilon-1)a\bar{x}_{0}<0$ , hence $f_{\rm quad}(x_{1}^{\rm Muon})<f_{\rm quad}(ax_{0})$ , which implies $\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X_{1}^{\rm Muon})<\mathcal{F}_{\rm quad}(X_{0})$ .

#### Step 2: Muon overshoots after two steps.

The second Muon momentum in river coordinates equals

$$ \displaystyle m_{2}^{\rm Muon} \displaystyle=\xi(\xi m_{0}+ax_{0})+x_{1}^{\rm Muon}=\xi^{2}m_{0}+a(1+\xi)x_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1} \displaystyle=\xi^{2}m_{0}+a\left[(1+\xi)x_{0}-(1+\varepsilon)\bar{x}_{0}\,\mathbf{1}\right]. $$

By assumption (58), $m_{2}^{\rm Muon}\succ\mathbf{0}$ , hence again $\mathtt{sign}(m_{2}^{\rm Muon})=\mathbf{1}$ and

$$ x_{2}^{\rm Muon}=x_{1}^{\rm Muon}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1}=ax_{0}-2\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1}. $$

Expanding as before,

$$ \displaystyle f_{\rm quad}(x_{2}^{\rm Muon})-f_{\rm quad}(ax_{0}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\|ax_{0}-2\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1}\|_{2}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\|ax_{0}\|_{2}^{2}=-2\eta^{\rm Muon}\,a\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}x_{0}+\frac{(2\eta^{\rm Muon})^{2}}{2}\,\|\mathbf{1}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle=-2\eta^{\rm Muon}\,a\,n\bar{x}_{0}+2(\eta^{\rm Muon})^{2}n=2n\eta^{\rm Muon}a\bar{x}_{0}\left(\frac{\eta^{\rm Muon}}{a\bar{x}_{0}}-1\right). $$

Because $\eta^{\rm Muon}=(1+\varepsilon)a\bar{x}_{0}>a\bar{x}_{0}$ , the last factor is positive; thus $f_{\rm quad}(x_{2}^{\rm Muon})>f_{\rm quad}(ax_{0})$ , which yields the overshoot claim (59).

#### Step 3: two-step decrease for momentum GD with a small constant step size.

Now consider the momentum-GD recursion

$$ \displaystyle m_{1}^{\rm GD}=\xi m_{0}+ax_{0}, \displaystyle\qquad x_{1}^{\rm GD}=ax_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}m_{1}^{\rm GD}, \displaystyle m_{2}^{\rm GD}=\xi m_{1}^{\rm GD}+x_{1}^{\rm GD}, \displaystyle\qquad x_{2}^{\rm GD}=x_{1}^{\rm GD}-\eta^{\rm GD}m_{2}^{\rm GD}. $$

A straightforward elimination gives

$$ x_{2}^{\rm GD}=ax_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}\Bigl[\xi(1+\xi)m_{0}+(2+\xi)ax_{0}\Bigr]+(\eta^{\rm GD})^{2}(\xi m_{0}+ax_{0}). $$

Define the $a$ -independent vectors $u:=x_{0}$ and $v:=m_{0}/a$ , so that $\|v\|_{2}\leq C_{m}$ and (61) can be rewritten as

$$ x_{2}^{\rm GD}=a\left[u-\eta^{\rm GD}\bigl(\xi(1+\xi)v+(2+\xi)u\bigr)+(\eta^{\rm GD})^{2}(\xi v+u)\right]. $$

Let $q(\eta):=u-\eta\bigl(\xi(1+\xi)v+(2+\xi)u\bigr)+\eta^{2}(\xi v+u)$ , so that $x_{2}^{\rm GD}=a\,q(\eta^{\rm GD})$ and

$$ f_{\rm quad}(x_{2}^{\rm GD})-f_{\rm quad}(ax_{0})=\frac{a^{2}}{2}\Bigl(\|q(\eta^{\rm GD})\|_{2}^{2}-\|u\|_{2}^{2}\Bigr). $$

Expanding $\|q(\eta)\|_{2}^{2}$ around $\eta=0$ gives

$$ \|q(\eta)\|_{2}^{2}=\|u\|_{2}^{2}-2\eta\,\left\langle u,\xi(1+\xi)v+(2+\xi)u\right\rangle+\eta^{2}\,R(\eta), $$

where $R(\eta)$ is a polynomial in $\eta$ whose coefficients are bounded in terms of $(\xi,\|u\|_{2},\|v\|_{2})$ . Using $u=x_{0}\succ\mathbf{0}$ and $v=m_{0}/a\succ\mathbf{0}$ , we have

$$ \left\langle u,\xi(1+\xi)v+(2+\xi)u\right\rangle\geq(2+\xi)\|u\|_{2}^{2}. $$

Moreover, there exists a constant $\bar{C}_{m}=\bar{C}_{m}(\xi,\|u\|_{2},C_{m})$ such that $|R(\eta)|\leq\bar{C}_{m}$ for all $\eta\in[0,1]$ (e.g., by bounding $\|q(\eta)\|_{2}$ and its coefficients via triangle inequality). Therefore, for every $\eta\in(0,1]$ ,

$$ \|q(\eta)\|_{2}^{2}-\|u\|_{2}^{2}\leq-2(2+\xi)\eta\|u\|_{2}^{2}+\bar{C}_{m}\eta^{2}. $$

Choose

$$ \eta_{0}:=\min\left\{1,\;\frac{(2+\xi)\|u\|_{2}^{2}}{\bar{C}_{m}}\right\}=\min\left\{1,\;\frac{(2+\xi)\|x_{0}\|_{2}^{2}}{\bar{C}_{m}}\right\}, $$

then for any $0<\eta^{\rm GD}\leq\eta_{0}$ we have $\|q(\eta^{\rm GD})\|_{2}^{2}-\|u\|_{2}^{2}<0$ , which implies $f_{\rm quad}(x_{2}^{\rm GD})<f_{\rm quad}(ax_{0})$ and hence (60). ∎

#### B.3.2 Late-stage overshoot for general smooth objectives

We now move from the exact quadratic toy model to a local theorem for general smooth objectives. The proof is carried out inside a late-stage spectral-river tube, where the iterate, gradient, and momentum admit a river-hill decomposition and the hill component remains small. In this regime, Muon’s $\mathtt{msign}$ update behaves as an almost-constant river sign step, so the two-step overshoot mechanism from the quadratic model persists up to perturbative errors.

#### River-dominated momentum.

We first explain why a river-dominated momentum state is natural in the late stage. Intuitively, once the iterates enter a spectral-river tube, the gradients become predominantly supported on the river subspace, with only small hill components. Since the stored momentum is formed as an exponential moving average (EMA) of recent gradients, it should therefore inherit the same river–hill structure. The following lemma makes this inheritance precise.

#### Lemma B.13 (EMA momentum remains river-dominated in a tube).

Suppose that at a reference time $0$ the stored momentum is an exponential moving average (EMA) over a window of length $L$ :

$$ M_{0}=\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{-j})+\xi^{L}M_{-L},\qquad 0\leq\xi<1. $$

Assume that along this window the gradients admit decompositions

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{-j})=\mathcal{B}(g_{j})+E_{j}^{g},\quad g_{j}\succ\mathbf{0},\quad\|g_{j}\|_{2}\leq\overline{C}_{g}a,\quad\min_{i}[g_{j}]_{i}\geq\underline{C}_{g}a,\quad\|E_{j}^{g}\|_{F}\leq\tau_{g}a, $$

for constants $\overline{C}_{g},\underline{C}_{g}>0$ and $\tau_{g}\geq 0$ independent of $a$ . Assume also that the old momentum satisfies

$$ \|M_{-L}\|_{F}\leq C_{M}a,\qquad\|\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L})\|_{F}\leq\tau_{m}a, $$

for constants $C_{M}<\infty$ and $\tau_{m}\geq 0$ independent of $a$ . Then $M_{0}$ admits a decomposition $M_{0}=\mathcal{B}(m_{0})+E_{0}^{m}$ with $E_{0}^{m}\in\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}^{\perp}$ , where

$$ \displaystyle m_{0} \displaystyle=\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}g_{j}+\xi^{L}\,\mathcal{B}^{-1}\!\bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})\bigr), \displaystyle E_{0}^{m} \displaystyle=\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}E_{j}^{g}+\xi^{L}\,\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L}). $$

Here, $\mathcal{B}^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\mathcal{B}$ restricted to the river subspace. Consequently,

$$ \|m_{0}\|_{2}\leq\overline{C}_{g}a\frac{1-\xi^{L}}{1-\xi}+C_{M}\xi^{L}a,\qquad\min_{i}[m_{0}]_{i}\geq\underline{C}_{g}a\frac{1-\xi^{L}}{1-\xi}-C_{M}\xi^{L}a, $$

and

$$ \|E_{0}^{m}\|_{F}\leq\tau_{g}a\frac{1-\xi^{L}}{1-\xi}+\tau_{m}\xi^{L}a. $$

#### Proof.

We decompose every term in the EMA formula into its river component and its hill component. For each $j=1,\cdots,L$ , the assumed gradient decomposition is

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{-j})=\mathcal{B}(g_{j})+E_{j}^{g},\qquad E_{j}^{g}\in\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}^{\perp}. $$

Similarly, decompose the old momentum as

$$ M_{-L}=\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})+\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L}), $$

where $\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})\in\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}$ and $\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L})\in\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}^{\perp}$ .

Substituting these decompositions into the EMA representation of $M_{0}$ and using the linearity of $\mathcal{B}$ and of the orthogonal projections, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle M_{0} \displaystyle=\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}\bigl(\mathcal{B}(g_{j})+E_{j}^{g}\bigr)+\xi^{L}\Bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})+\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L})\Bigr) \displaystyle=\mathcal{B}\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}g_{j}+\xi^{L}\,\mathcal{B}^{-1}\!\bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})\bigr)\right)+\left(\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}E_{j}^{g}+\xi^{L}\,\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L})\right). $$

Therefore $M_{0}$ admits the decomposition $M_{0}=\mathcal{B}(m_{0})+E_{0}^{m}$ , where $m_{0}$ is (62) and $E_{0}^{m}$ is (63). Because each $E_{j}^{g}$ and $\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L})$ lies in $\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}^{\perp}$ , the same is true for their weighted sum, i.e., $E_{0}^{m}\in\mathtt{span}\{B_{1},\cdots,B_{n}\}^{\perp}$ as well.

It remains to verify the stated bounds.

First, since $\mathcal{B}$ is an isometric identification between $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and the river subspace, we have

$$ \bigl\|\mathcal{B}^{-1}\!\bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(Y)\bigr)\bigr\|_{2}=\|\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(Y)\|_{F}\leq\|Y\|_{F}\qquad\text{for every matrix }Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}. $$

Hence, using the triangle inequality together with the assumptions on $g_{j}$ and $M_{-L}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\|m_{0}\|_{2} \displaystyle\leq\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}\|g_{j}\|_{2}+\xi^{L}\bigl\|\mathcal{B}^{-1}\!\bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})\bigr)\bigr\|_{2}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}\overline{C}_{g}a+\xi^{L}\|M_{-L}\|_{F} \displaystyle\leq\overline{C}_{g}a\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}+C_{M}\xi^{L}a=\overline{C}_{g}a\frac{1-\xi^{L}}{1-\xi}+C_{M}\xi^{L}a. $$

Next, we prove the coordinatewise lower bound. Fix any coordinate $i$ . By the definition of $m_{0}$ ,

$$ [m_{0}]_{i}=\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}[g_{j}]_{i}+\xi^{L}\left[\mathcal{B}^{-1}\!\bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})\bigr)\right]_{i}. $$

Using the lower bound on $[g_{j}]_{i}$ and the estimate

$$ \left|\left[\mathcal{B}^{-1}\!\bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})\bigr)\right]_{i}\right|\leq\bigl\|\mathcal{B}^{-1}\!\bigl(\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(M_{-L})\bigr)\bigr\|_{2}\leq\|M_{-L}\|_{F}\leq C_{M}a, $$

we obtain

$$ [m_{0}]_{i}\geq\underline{C}_{g}a\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}-C_{M}\xi^{L}a=\underline{C}_{g}a\frac{1-\xi^{L}}{1-\xi}-C_{M}\xi^{L}a. $$

Since this bound is uniform in $i$ , it follows that

$$ \min_{i}[m_{0}]_{i}\geq\underline{C}_{g}a\frac{1-\xi^{L}}{1-\xi}-C_{M}\xi^{L}a. $$

Finally, for the off-river hill remainder, the triangle inequality gives

$$ \displaystyle\|E_{0}^{m}\|_{F}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}\|E_{j}^{g}\|_{F}+\xi^{L}\|\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}^{\perp}}(M_{-L})\|_{F}\leq\tau_{g}a\sum_{j=1}^{L}\xi^{j-1}+\tau_{m}\xi^{L}a=\tau_{g}a\frac{1-\xi^{L}}{1-\xi}+\tau_{m}\xi^{L}a. $$

This proves the stated bound on $E_{0}^{m}$ and completes the proof. ∎

#### Structural hypotheses.

We now state the structural hypotheses used in Theorem B.18.

The first assumption is standard: it requires a nondegenerate local minimizer together with quantitative Taylor control near $X^{\star}$ .

#### Assumption B.14 (Local quadratic model with third-order control).

The objective $\mathcal{F}:\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ is $C^{3}$ in a neighborhood of $X^{\star}$ , and $\nabla\mathcal{F}(X^{\star})=0$ . Write $H_{\star}:=\nabla^{2}\mathcal{F}(X^{\star})$ . There exist constants $0<\underline{L}\leq\overline{L}<\infty$ such that

$$ \underline{L}\|Y\|_{F}^{2}\leq\langle Y,H_{\star}[Y]\rangle\leq\overline{L}\|Y\|_{F}^{2}\qquad\text{for all }Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}. $$

Moreover, for some constant $C_{3}<\infty$ and all sufficiently small $Y$ ,

$$ \|\nabla\mathcal{F}(X^{\star}+Y)-H_{\star}[Y]\|_{F}\leq C_{3}\|Y\|_{F}^{2}, $$

and

$$ \left|\mathcal{F}(X^{\star}+Y)-\mathcal{F}(X^{\star})-\langle Y,H_{\star}[Y]\rangle/2\right|\leq C_{3}\|Y\|_{F}^{3}. $$

#### Assumption B.15 (Hessian river-to-hill leakage bound).

Let $K$ be the matrix introduced earlier (see B.7) and assume $K\succ 0$ . There exist constants $C_{y}<\infty$ and $\tau_{h}\geq 0$ such that for every $y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with $\|y\|_{2}\leq C_{y}$ ,

$$ H_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(y)]=\mathcal{B}(Ky)+E^{h}(y),\qquad\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(E^{h}(y))=0,\qquad\|E^{h}(y)\|_{F}\leq\tau_{h}\|y\|_{2}. $$

#### Assumption B.16 (Late-stage initialization inside a tube).

Let $a>0$ . Assume the initial iterate decomposes as

$$ X_{0}=X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(ax_{0})+E_{0}^{x},\qquad\mathtt{Proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(E_{0}^{x})=0,\qquad\|E_{0}^{x}\|_{F}\leq\tau_{x}a, $$

for some $x_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ satisfying $Kx_{0}\succ\mathbf{0}$ . Assume the stored momentum decomposes as

$$ M_{0}=\mathcal{B}(m_{0})+E_{0}^{m},\qquad\|m_{0}\|_{2}\leq C_{m}a,\qquad\|E_{0}^{m}\|_{F}\leq\tau_{m}a, $$

for constants $C_{m}<\infty$ and $\tau_{m}\geq 0$ independent of $a$ .

#### Lemma B.17 (Polar stability near a positive river matrix).

Let $y\succ\mathbf{0}$ and define $Y=\mathcal{B}(y)+E^{y}$ . If $\|E^{y}\|_{2}\leq\frac{1}{2}\min_{i}[y]_{i}$ , then $Y$ has full column rank, and

$$ \|\mathtt{msign}(Y)-\mathtt{msign}(\mathcal{B}(y))\|_{F}\leq\frac{4}{3\,\min_{i}[y]_{i}}\|E^{y}\|_{F}. $$

#### Proof.

The unperturbed matrix $\mathcal{B}(y)=U_{\star}\mathtt{Diag}(y)V_{\star}^{\top}$ has singular values exactly $[y]_{1},\cdots,[y]_{n}$ , and hence $\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal{B}(y))=\min_{i}[y]_{i}$ . By Weyl’s inequality [60],

$$ \sigma_{\min}(Y)\geq\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal{B}(y))-\|E^{y}\|_{2}\geq\frac{1}{2}\min_{i}[y]_{i}>0, $$

so $Y$ has full column rank.

We now apply the standard perturbation bound for the unit polar factor of full-column-rank matrices:

$$ \|\mathtt{msign}(Y)-\mathtt{msign}(\mathcal{B}(y))\|_{F}\leq\frac{2}{\sigma_{\min}(Y)+\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal{B}(y))}\|E^{y}\|_{F}. $$

Using the lower bounds above gives

$$ \frac{2}{\sigma_{\min}(Y)+\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal{B}(y))}\leq\frac{2}{\frac{1}{2}\min_{i}[y]_{i}+\min_{i}[y]_{i}}=\frac{4}{3\min_{i}[y]_{i}}, $$

and therefore

$$ \|\mathtt{msign}(Y)-\mathtt{msign}(\mathcal{B}(y))\|_{F}\leq\frac{4}{3\min_{i}[y]_{i}}\|E^{y}\|_{F}. $$

This proves the claim. ∎

#### Local step size and positivity margins.

Define

$$ y_{0}:=\frac{\mathbf{1}^{\top}Kx_{0}}{\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\eta^{\rm Muon}:=(1+\varepsilon)ay_{0}, $$

where $0<\varepsilon<1$ is fixed. Define the scaled positivity margins

$$ \kappa_{1}:=\min_{i}\frac{\xi[m_{0}]_{i}+a[Kx_{0}]_{i}}{a}, $$

and

$$ \kappa_{2}:=\min_{i}\left[\frac{\xi\bigl(\xi m_{0}+aKx_{0}\bigr)+aK\bigl(x_{0}-(1+\varepsilon)y_{0}\mathbf{1}\bigr)}{a}\right]_{i}. $$

#### Theorem B.18 (Late-stage Muon overshoot along the spectral river (two-steps analysis)).

Assume Assumptions B.14, B.15, and B.16. Fix $\xi\in(0,1)$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ , and define $\eta^{\rm Muon}$ by (69). Assume that $\kappa_{1}$ and $\kappa_{2}$ defined in (70) and (71) are bounded below by positive constants independent of $a$ . Then there exist constants $a_{0}>0$ , $\tau^{h}_{0}>0$ , $\tau^{m}_{0}>0$ , $\tau^{x}_{0}>0$ , and $\eta_{0}>0$ (depending only on the local constants and on $(K,\xi,x_{0},C_{m},\varepsilon)$ , but not on $a$ ) such that whenever

$$ 0<a\leq a_{0},\qquad 0\leq\tau_{h}\leq\tau^{h}_{0},\qquad 0\leq\tau_{m}\leq\tau^{m}_{0},\qquad 0\leq\tau_{x}\leq\tau^{x}_{0}, $$

the Muon iterates and momentum-GD iterates initialized from the same pair $(X_{0},M_{0})$ satisfy

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{1}^{\rm Muon})<\mathcal{F}(X_{0})<\mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm Muon}),\qquad\mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm GD})<\mathcal{F}(X_{0}), $$

for every GD step size $0<\eta^{\rm GD}\leq\eta_{0}$ . In particular, since $\eta^{\rm Muon}=O(a)$ while $\eta_{0}=O(1)$ , we have $\eta^{\rm Muon}<\eta_{0}$ for all sufficiently small $a$ .

#### Proof.

We prove (72) in three steps.

#### Step 1: first Muon step decreases.

From (66), write $Y_{0}:=X_{0}-X^{\star}=\mathcal{B}(ax_{0})+E_{0}^{x}$ with $\|E_{0}^{x}\|_{F}\leq\tau_{x}a$ . Assumption B.14 gives

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=H_{\star}[Y_{0}]+E^{g}_{0},\qquad\|E^{g}_{0}\|_{F}\leq C_{3}\|Y_{0}\|_{F}^{2}. $$

Using (65) with $y=ax_{0}$ , linearity of $H_{\star}$ , and (64), we obtain

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=a\,\mathcal{B}(Kx_{0})+E_{0}^{\nabla},\qquad\|E_{0}^{\nabla}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}(\tau_{h}+\tau_{x})a+\bar{C}a^{2}, $$

where $\bar{C}$ depends only on the local constants and on $\|x_{0}\|_{2}$ . Throughout this proof, $\bar{C}$ denotes a generic positive constant, possibly changing from line to line, whose value depends only on fixed problem constants and is independent of $a$ , $\tau_{h}$ , $\tau_{m}$ , and $\tau_{x}$ . Combining the result with (67) yields

$$ M_{1}^{\rm Muon}=\xi M_{0}+\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=\mathcal{B}\bigl(\xi m_{0}+aKx_{0}\bigr)+E_{1}^{m},\quad\|E_{1}^{m}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}(\tau_{m}+\tau_{h}+\tau_{x})a+\bar{C}a^{2}. $$

By (70),

$$ \min_{i}[\xi m_{0}+aKx_{0}]_{i}\geq a\kappa_{1}. $$

Thus, shrinking $a_{0},\tau^{h}_{0},\tau^{m}_{0},\tau^{x}_{0}$ if needed so that $\|E_{1}^{m}\|_{2}\leq\frac{1}{2}a\kappa_{1}$ , Lemma B.17 implies

$$ \mathtt{msign}(M_{1}^{\rm Muon})=\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{1})+\Delta_{1},\quad\|\Delta_{1}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}(\tau_{m}+\tau_{h}+\tau_{x}+a). $$

Hence with $\|E_{1}^{x}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}a(\tau_{m}+\tau_{h}+\tau_{x}+a)$ , we have

$$ X_{1}^{\rm Muon}=X_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathtt{msign}(M_{1}^{\rm Muon})=X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(ax_{0}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1})+E_{1}^{x}. $$

Using the loss expansion in Assumption B.14 at $X^{\star}$ and the identity

$$ \langle\mathcal{B}(y),H_{\star}[\mathcal{B}(y)]\rangle=y^{\top}Ky+\langle\mathcal{B}(y),E^{h}(y)\rangle=y^{\top}Ky, $$

we obtain

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{1}^{\rm Muon})-\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=-\eta^{\rm Muon}a\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}Kx_{0}+\frac{1}{2}(\eta^{\rm Muon})^{2}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}+O\!\left(a^{2}(\tau_{m}+\tau_{h}+\tau_{x}+a)\right). $$

Substituting $\eta^{\rm Muon}=(1+\varepsilon)ay_{0}$ and $\mathbf{1}^{\top}Kx_{0}=y_{0}\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}$ yields a strictly negative leading term:

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{1}^{\rm Muon})-\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=-\frac{1}{2}(1-\varepsilon^{2})a^{2}y_{0}^{2}\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}+O\!\left(a^{2}(\tau_{m}+\tau_{h}+\tau_{x}+a)\right). $$

Choosing $a_{0},\tau^{h}_{0},\tau^{m}_{0},\tau^{x}_{0}$ so that the error term is dominated by the leading negative term gives

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{1}^{\rm Muon})<\mathcal{F}(X_{0}). $$

#### Step 2: second Muon step overshoots.

Repeat the previous gradient expansion at $X_{1}^{\rm Muon}$ . From the representation of $X_{1}^{\rm Muon}-X^{\star}$ and Assumptions B.14–B.15, we obtain

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{1}^{\rm Muon})=a\,\mathcal{B}\bigl(K(x_{0}-(1+\varepsilon)y_{0}\mathbf{1})\bigr)+E_{1}^{\nabla},\quad\|E_{1}^{\nabla}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}(\tau_{h}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{x})a+\bar{C}a^{2}. $$

Therefore

$$ M_{2}^{\rm Muon}=\xi M_{1}^{\rm Muon}+\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{1}^{\rm Muon})=\mathcal{B}(\bar{m}_{1})+E_{2}^{m},\quad\|E_{2}^{m}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}(\tau_{h}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{x})a+\bar{C}a^{2}, $$

where

$$ \bar{m}_{1}:=\xi(\xi m_{0}+aKx_{0})+aK\bigl(x_{0}-(1+\varepsilon)y_{0}\mathbf{1}\bigr). $$

By (71), we know $\min_{i}[\bar{m}_{1}]_{i}\geq a\kappa_{2}$ . Shrinking $a_{0},\tau^{h}_{0},\tau^{m}_{0},\tau^{x}_{0}$ if necessary so that $\|E_{2}^{m}\|_{2}\leq\frac{1}{2}a\kappa_{2}$ , Lemma B.17 yields

$$ \mathtt{msign}(M_{2}^{\rm Muon})=\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{1})+\Delta_{2},\quad\|\Delta_{2}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}(\tau_{h}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{x}+a). $$

Hence with $\|E_{2}^{x}\|_{F}\leq\bar{C}a(\tau_{h}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{x}+a)$ , we have

$$ X_{2}^{\rm Muon}=X_{1}^{\rm Muon}-\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathtt{msign}(M_{2}^{\rm Muon})=X^{\star}+\mathcal{B}(ax_{0}-2\eta^{\rm Muon}\mathbf{1})+E_{2}^{x}. $$

Using again the loss expansion around $X^{\star}$ and the leakage bound (65), we obtain

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm Muon})-\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=-2\eta^{\rm Muon}a\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}Kx_{0}+2(\eta^{\rm Muon})^{2}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}+O\!\left(a^{2}(\tau_{h}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{x}+a)\right). $$

Substituting $\eta^{\rm Muon}=(1+\varepsilon)ay_{0}$ and $\mathbf{1}^{\top}Kx_{0}=y_{0}\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}$ yields a strictly positive leading term:

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm Muon})-\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=2\varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)a^{2}y_{0}^{2}\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}+O\!\left(a^{2}(\tau_{h}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{x}+a)\right). $$

Choosing $a_{0},\tau^{h}_{0},\tau^{m}_{0},\tau^{x}_{0}$ sufficiently small ensures the error term is dominated by the positive leading term, hence

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm Muon})>\mathcal{F}(X_{0}). $$

#### Step 3: two-step momentum GD decreases for a small constant step size.

Consider momentum GD initialized from the same $(X_{0},M_{0})$ :

$$ \displaystyle M_{1}^{\rm GD}=\xi M_{0}+\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{0}),\qquad \displaystyle X_{1}^{\rm GD}=X_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}M_{1}^{\rm GD}, \displaystyle M_{2}^{\rm GD}=\xi M_{1}^{\rm GD}+\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{1}^{\rm GD}),\qquad \displaystyle X_{2}^{\rm GD}=X_{1}^{\rm GD}-\eta^{\rm GD}M_{2}^{\rm GD}. $$

We show that there exists $\eta_{0}=O(1)$ such that $\mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm GD})<\mathcal{F}(X_{0})$ for all $0<\eta^{\rm GD}\leq\eta_{0}$ and all sufficiently small $(a,\tau_{h},\tau_{m},\tau_{x})$ .

Define the quadratic model function

$$ Q(Y):=\frac{1}{2}\langle Y,H_{\star}[Y]\rangle. $$

By Assumption B.14, for all iterates staying in the local neighborhood,

$$ \mathcal{F}(X^{\star}+Y)=\mathcal{F}(X^{\star})+Q(Y)+O(\|Y\|_{F}^{3}), $$

and

$$ \nabla\mathcal{F}(X^{\star}+Y)=H_{\star}[Y]+O(\|Y\|_{F}^{2}). $$

Since $X_{0}-X^{\star}=O(a)$ and we only take two steps with $\eta^{\rm GD}=O(1)$ , by choosing $a_{0}$ sufficiently small we ensure $\|X_{t}^{\rm GD}-X^{\star}\|_{F}=O(a)$ for $t=0,1,2$ , and thus the Taylor remainders contribute at most $O(a^{3})$ to function values and $O(a^{2})$ to gradients.

We now compare the true two-step map with the quadratic dynamics obtained by replacing $\nabla\mathcal{F}(X)$ by $H_{\star}[X-X^{\star}]$ . Let $\tilde{X}_{t}$ denote this quadratic two-step sequence (initialized at the same $\tilde{X}_{0}=X_{0}$ and $\tilde{M}_{0}=M_{0}$ ):

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{M}_{1}=\xi\tilde{M}_{0}+H_{\star}[\tilde{X}_{0}-X^{\star}],\qquad \displaystyle\tilde{X}_{1}=\tilde{X}_{0}-\eta^{\rm GD}\tilde{M}_{1}, \displaystyle\tilde{M}_{2}=\xi\tilde{M}_{1}+H_{\star}[\tilde{X}_{1}-X^{\star}],\qquad \displaystyle\tilde{X}_{2}=\tilde{X}_{1}-\eta^{\rm GD}\tilde{M}_{2}. $$

Because all operators are linear in this quadratic model, $\tilde{X}_{2}-X^{\star}$ is an affine polynomial in $\eta^{\rm GD}$ whose coefficients depend continuously on $(\tilde{X}_{0}-X^{\star},\tilde{M}_{0})$ . In particular, the map $\eta^{\rm GD}\mapsto Q(\tilde{X}_{2}-X^{\star})$ is a polynomial in $\eta^{\rm GD}$ .

We claim that the directional derivative at $\eta^{\rm GD}=0$ is strictly negative uniformly over all admissible $(X_{0},M_{0})$ in Assumption B.16. At $\eta^{\rm GD}=0$ , we have $\tilde{X}_{1}=\tilde{X}_{0}$ and hence

$$ \left.\frac{d}{d\eta^{\rm GD}}Q(\tilde{X}_{2}-X^{\star})\right|_{\eta^{\rm GD}=0}=-\left\langle\tilde{X}_{0}-X^{\star},\;H_{\star}\!\left[\xi(1+\xi)\tilde{M}_{0}+(2+\xi)H_{\star}[\tilde{X}_{0}-X^{\star}]\right]\right\rangle. $$

Using $\tilde{X}_{0}-X^{\star}=\mathcal{B}(ax_{0})+E_{0}^{x}$ and $\tilde{M}_{0}=\mathcal{B}(m_{0})+E_{0}^{m}$ , expand the inner products. The leading river contribution equals

$$ -a^{2}(2+\xi)\,(Kx_{0})^{\top}Kx_{0}-a\,\xi(1+\xi)\,(Kx_{0})^{\top}m_{0}, $$

which is strictly negative because $K\succ 0$ , $Kx_{0}\succ\mathbf{0}$ , and $m_{0}$ is $O(a)$ with nonnegative coordinates in the late-stage regime (captured by the positivity margin in (70)). All remaining terms involve at least one hill component ( $E_{0}^{x}$ or $E_{0}^{m}$ ) and are therefore bounded by

$$ O\!\left(a^{2}(\tau_{x}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{h})\right), $$

using (64), (65), and Cauchy–Schwarz. Thus, for sufficiently small $\tau_{x}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{h}$ , the derivative remains strictly negative uniformly over the admissible set.

Since $Q(\tilde{X}_{2}-X^{\star})$ is a polynomial in $\eta^{\rm GD}$ with coefficients bounded uniformly over the admissible set (because $\|X_{0}-X^{\star}\|_{F}=O(a)$ , $\|M_{0}\|_{F}=O(a)$ , and $H_{\star}$ is bounded), there exists $\eta_{0}>0$ independent of $a$ such that

$$ Q(\tilde{X}_{2}-X^{\star})<Q(X_{0}-X^{\star})\qquad\text{for all }0<\eta^{\rm GD}\leq\eta_{0}. $$

Finally, the difference between the true iterate $X_{2}^{\rm GD}$ and the quadratic iterate $\tilde{X}_{2}$ over two steps is $O(a^{2})$ in norm, because each gradient differs from its linearization by $O(a^{2})$ and the step size is $O(1)$ . Therefore,

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm GD})-\mathcal{F}(X_{0})=\left(Q(\widetilde{X}_{2}-X^{\star})-Q(X_{0}-X^{\star})\right)+O\!\left(a^{2}(\tau_{h}+\tau_{m}+\tau_{x})+a^{3}\right), $$

and by shrinking $a_{0},\tau^{h}_{0},\tau^{m}_{0},\tau^{x}_{0}$ if necessary, the negative quadratic decrease dominates the perturbation, giving

$$ \mathcal{F}(X_{2}^{\rm GD})<\mathcal{F}(X_{0})\qquad\text{for all }0<\eta^{\rm GD}\leq\eta_{0}. $$

Combining Steps 1–3 proves (72). ∎

### B.4 Implications for Algorithm Design

#### B.4.1 Late-stage Adam behaves more like gradient methods than Muon

We finally record an Adam-like comparison. The purpose of this proposition is not to analyze the full Adam recursion, but rather to show that, once the diagonal preconditioner has stabilized, the resulting short-horizon behavior is qualitatively closer to gradient-based refinement than to Muon’s sign-type dynamics. As a transparent late-stage surrogate for Adam, we consider a momentum method with a frozen positive diagonal preconditioner:

$$ M_{t+1}^{\rm Adam}=\xi M_{t}^{\rm Adam}+\nabla\mathcal{F}(X_{t}^{\rm Adam}),\qquad X_{t+1}^{\rm Adam}=X_{t}^{\rm Adam}-\eta^{\rm Adam}P^{-1}M_{t+1}^{\rm Adam}, $$

where

$$ P=\mathtt{Diag}(p_{1},\cdots,p_{n^{2}}),\qquad 0<\underline{p}\leq p_{i}\leq\overline{p},\qquad i=1,2,\cdots,n^{2}. $$

This model is intended to approximate the late-stage behavior of Adam over a short time horizon after the second-moment denominator has effectively stabilized.
